pitch: with mouthpiece from #1579, B-natural, slide fully closed; with slide extended approx. 44mm, B-flat, somewhat sharp.
dimensions: diam of mouthpipe opening 9, bo1 10.2, bo2 11, be 95,le 2588, h 1065
literature: Paganuzzi et al 1976: 156 (photo); Van der Meer & Weber 1982: 70–72, 128 (photo); Fischer 1984: 43; Paganuzzi 1987: 24–29 (photos).
remarks: Flat slide-stays;¹ two undecorated hooks with eyelets on immoveable stay; sleeves attaching slide stays to descending slide tube decorated with head of a man and of a boy. Rings in slide-bow and bell- bow. Flat bell-stay with oriental motif;²  sleeve attaching bell-stay to neck-pipe may not be original.³  Rings in slide- and bell-bows. Ball or knob in bell-pipe in manner of trumpet. Little terminal flare in bell. The instrument appears to be of Nuremberg manufacture; if it is Venetian, as Van der Meer & Weber claim, it is not only the oldest extant trombone of Italian manufacture, but also the only such instrument made prior to the beginning of the 19th century to survive. This is probably the instrument mentioned in the 1562 inventory of the Accademia Filarmonica.⁴   Examined by SC, March 2001.
footnotes: Van der Meer & Weber (1982: 70) state that the immoveable slide stay is missing, and indeed this observation is confirmed by the photo on p. 128. It was certainly on the instrument when I examined it in March 2001, however****.
